title: Small reductions in the psychological cost of initiating applications can sharply increase job search
source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11465, Why Don't Jobseekers Search More? Barriers and Returns to Search on a Job
geography: Jobseekers using a search platform in Pakistan, studied through an experiment changing the default process for initiating job applications

application_effect.unit: percent increase in applications after changing the default process for initiating applications

barrier.value: the intervention is consistent with psychological costs of initiating an application

search_outcome.value: small reductions in search costs can substantially improve search outcomes where some jobseekers are relatively inactive

observations.method: Randomized experiment changing the default application-initiation process on a Pakistani job-search platform.
observations.uncertainty: The result is specific to the platform, jobseekers, vacancy mix, interface, and intervention; a large application response does not establish a comparable increase in interviews, offers, employment, wages, or job quality.
observations.subgroup: Jobseekers with different confidence, information, digital access, time, prior search experience, perceived fit, and exposure to high-return vacancies.
observations.counterinterpretation: The intervention may have changed attention, salience, or interface convenience rather than only psychological cost; applications can increase without improving match quality or employer response.

denominator.unit: applications generated by the randomized interface change

returns_shape.value: marginal treatment-induced applications had approximately constant rather than decreasing returns

model_consistency.value: the pattern is consistent with a directed-search model in which some jobseekers miss high-return vacancies because initiating applications is costly

allocation_implication.value: the first visible barrier may be initiation and search allocation rather than the absence of vacancies or worker interest

observations.method: Experimental comparison of application behavior and marginal returns under a changed application default, interpreted through a directed-search model.
observations.uncertainty: The model interpretation does not identify every psychological, informational, financial, or institutional source of search cost, and it does not show how employers rank or respond to additional applications.
observations.subgroup: Relatively inactive jobseekers, applicants who would otherwise miss high-return vacancies, employers receiving applications, and people with different perceived fit or confidence.
observations.counterinterpretation: Constant marginal returns may reflect platform mechanics or vacancy composition rather than a general law of job-search behavior; application volume can also increase screening burden for employers.

observations.period: 2026 paper; job-search participation and policy design

denominator.unit: job-search intervention and directed-search policy frame

diagnostic_shift.value: low observed search can reflect avoidable initiation friction rather than low motivation

design_lever.value: default design and small reductions in search costs can be treated as labor-market policy levers

missing_outcomes.value: the experiment leaves employment, wages, job quality, retention, and employer-side match outcomes to further testing

observations.method: World Bank experimental evidence translated into a bounded labor-market design implication.
observations.uncertainty: The intervention does not resolve broader barriers such as transport, childcare, discrimination, credentials, wages, safety, or the availability of decent jobs.
observations.subgroup: People who face initiation, confidence, time, transport, care, information, or discrimination barriers; employers and public employment services that mediate search and matching.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reducing application friction can shift burden toward employers or produce more low-quality applications unless matching, screening, and worker protections improve together.

boundary: This record adds a causal application-initiation-to-search-participation route and a psychological/search-cost mechanism for jobseekers in Pakistan. It does not establish increased employment, wages, job quality, match quality, retention, employer welfare, generalization to other platforms or labor markets, or that interface defaults can substitute for decent jobs and structural access supports.
